topics.topic: Definition and enforcement value of the process-count limit, including the sandbox runner
questions: What exactly does `process_count` count, and what process limit is installed given that the sandbox runner itself is a process?
What exactly does `process_count` count, and what RLIMIT_NPROC value must the sandbox set when its runner is itself a process?
What exactly does `process_count` count: the runner plus how many code-created processes, and does the runner itself consume one unit of the declared bound?

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the runner's limit on the number of processes, process_count + 1, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).
judgement.why: The later note defines the counted tasks, includes the runner as the first, excludes bubblewrap, and fixes the outer process limit at process_count plus one.

topics.topic: Events and behaviors that qualify as a scratch-file limit hit
questions: What constitutes a scratch-limit hit when a write reaches the file-size limit, particularly if the write is short, raises an error that user code catches, or terminates the process via the file-size signal?
What constitutes a scratch limit hit when a write is refused or partial, the code catches the error, or the process receives or changes the disposition of the file-size signal?

What observable event counts as a scratch limit hit when a write crosses the file-size limit, particularly if Python receives and catches an error, restores the signal's default disposition, or completes a short or partial write?

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] A memory, scratch or output bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside — the parent kills an environment for its wall deadline alone, and a process killed by a signal, SIGXFSZ included, exited abnormally: a MemoryError or an OSError with errno EFBIG for a file past the file-size limit escaped run and reached the parent through the exchange channel, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes; code that catches such an error and returns is judged by what it returned, like any other output (owner, 2026-10-06). Only the process bound is also seen inside, because every thread start and os.fork passes the runner's audit hook.

Only EFBIG is a scratch hit; exhausted host storage (ENOSPC,
       EDQUOT) is an ordinary error, and code killed by SIGXFSZ after
       restoring its default exited abnormally — both `crashed` (round 116).
judgement.why: The later texts define an escaped EFBIG as the scratch hit, say a caught error is judged by the returned result, and classify termination by SIGXFSZ as an abnormal exit.

topics.topic: Outcome and isolation semantics when host storage exhaustion causes a scratch write failure
questions: If a scratch write fails because host storage is exhausted rather than because the configured scratch-file limit was reached, is that a scratch limit hit, an ordinary exception visible to the code, or a sandbox failure with another outcome?
If a scratch write fails because host storage is exhausted rather than because the per-file limit was reached, what outcome and isolation guarantee apply?

If a scratch write fails because host storage is exhausted rather than because the configured scratch limit was reached, is that `resource_exhausted`, an exception visible to the code and therefore possibly `crashed`, or an internal error?

quotes:
Only EFBIG is a scratch hit; exhausted host storage (ENOSPC,
       EDQUOT) is an ordinary error, and code killed by SIGXFSZ after
       restoring its default exited abnormally — both `crashed` (round 116).

execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] Agent code is untrusted: it MUST only ever run inside a fresh bubblewrap environment created for that one execution, never in the kernel process and never through a faster path, and the environment never receives a credential, a host path other than its own exchange directory and the read-only runtime the next note binds (A03 rule 1, decision 25), and the code never sees a variable outside the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant (the runner sets the environment to it before loading the code, as the bounds note says).
judgement.why: The later texts make host-storage exhaustion an ordinary sandboxed exception rather than a scratch hit, with crashed only if it escapes, while preserving the fresh bubblewrap isolation boundary.

topics.topic: Resource-limit values and limit-setting paths that the startup sandbox probe must verify
questions: Which resource-bound values must the startup probe install and verify, given that `probe_sandbox` takes no ResourceBounds input?
Which resource-bound values and limit-setting cases must `probe_sandbox` exercise before the kernel is allowed to start?
Which resource-bound values and limit-setting paths must the start probe exercise, and must failure to set any supported limit stop kernel startup?

quotes: probe_sandbox: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise SandboxUnavailableError naming what is missing when the bubblewrap executable, bwrap, cannot be found on the process's PATH, when bwrap --version, which prints "bubblewrap" and the version, names a version other than the imported RELEASE_BWRAP_VERSION constant, when the resolved interpreter path os.path.realpath(sys.executable) lies under no path of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant, when that interpreter, the one execute_function starts inside bubblewrap, run once through bwrap with the same read-only bindings of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant and the same links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant to print platform.python_implementation() and platform.python_version() joined by one space, does not print exactly the imported RELEASE_SANDBOX_INTERPRETER constant, or when one probe execution through execute_function of a minimal implementation with no ports, under bounds equal to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_WALL_TIME_MS, RELEASE_CEILING_MEMORY_BYTES, RELEASE_CEILING_OUTPUT_BYTES and RELEASE_CEILING_PROCESS_COUNT constants, does not end succeeded, naming its outcome.

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] The runner MUST set every setrlimit limit inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code, soft and hard alike (every limit is set soft and hard to the same value; bubblewrap is started without any capability option, so the code holds none and cannot raise a limit): address space at bounds.memory_bytes, the size of a file written in the scratch at the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, and the outer process bound, the limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1; a runner that cannot set one exits before it loads the code and the execution is crashed; probe_sandbox's probe execution runs the same runner with the current release ceilings, so a host that refuses them does not start, while an earlier contract version's larger bounds (A20 rule 4) are set only when it executes and are crashed where the host refuses them; the parent sets no setrlimit limit (the process bound:  the one is the task bubblewrap's init would be, and with the runner as the namespace's init it is the margin that keeps the outer bound above the audit hook's exact count; set by the parent, that limit would count every process of the user on the host and bubblewrap could not create its namespace (EAGAIN)), process_count itself being enforced by the runner's audit hook. The parent MUST enforce from outside a wall deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken when the environment starts plus bounds.wall_time_ms in nanoseconds and held in a local variable of execute_function only, after which — once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it — it kills every process of the environment by sending SIGKILL, through a pidfd, to the environment's PID-namespace init, the child-pid bubblewrap reports on --info-fd — not to bubblewrap itself or its process group — and then waits for bubblewrap to exit, and an output count, the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; output over a bound is a failure, never truncated.
judgement.why: The later contract fixes the probe's four ResourceBounds at the current release ceilings and requires the same runner to install all setrlimit limits, so any unsupported limit prevents a successful probe and stops startup.

topics.topic: Whether scratch storage requires an aggregate directory byte limit in addition to per-file limits
questions: Is there an aggregate size bound for the exchange directory, or is only each individual scratch file bounded?
Is only each individual scratch file bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`, or must the exchange directory also have an aggregate byte bound?
Is scratch bounded only per file, or must the sandbox also enforce a total byte bound for the exchange directory?

quotes:
The scratch bound is the host
       kernel's file-size limit on every file the code writes (the runner
       ignores SIGXFSZ, so the write fails with EFBIG); the exchange directory
       as a whole has no separate bound in this release.
judgement.why: The later contract explicitly chooses a per-file scratch bound and no aggregate exchange-directory bound.

topics.topic: Required relationship between installed soft and hard resource limits
questions: Must every applicable soft and hard resource limit be set to the same specified bound, or may the sandbox choose different soft and hard values while preventing code from raising the effective limit?
